title: The Quran: Surah 103, al-'Asr (Time)
author: Tradução inglesa de Talal Itani (ClearQuran)
tradition: Texto sagrado do Islão, século VII
intro: Lição sobre a Surata 103. O texto inglês é a tradução de Talal Itani, reproduzida sem alterações; as notas de língua, perguntas, discussão e escrita são material pedagógico separado, baseado apenas no que o próprio texto diz.

source.title: Quran English Translation: Clear, Pure, Easy to Read Modern English
source.edition: Edition A (uses the word 'Allah' to refer to the Creator)

questions.q: According to verse 2, what is the human being in?
questions.why: O versículo 2 diz: 'The human being is in loss.'

options: people who are left out of the statement in verse 2
questions.why: 'Except those who...' nomeia quem fica de fora do que se diz no versículo 2.

questions.q: What does the word 'except' tell us about verse 2?
options: That it is true for everyone apart from the group in verse 3
That it is not true for anyone
That it is about the past
questions.why: A excepção do versículo 3 limita a afirmação geral do versículo 2.

questions.q: Verse 3 is a list joined by 'and'. How many actions does it list?
questions.why: O versículo 3 lista quatro: believe, do good works, encourage truth, recommend patience.

questions.q: Which sentence best sums up the passage?
options: The human being is in loss, except those who do four things
The human being is in danger from a storm
The human being has no work
questions.why: O versículo 2 afirma a perda e o versículo 3 dá a excepção.

B2.discussion: The passage is only 22 words long. What can a very short text do that a long text cannot?
B2.writing: Write 80 to 100 words: Explain in your own words what verses 2 and 3 say.

options: Those who believe, do good works, encourage truth and recommend patience
questions.why: O versículo 3 nomeia quem acredita, faz boas obras, encoraja a verdade e recomenda a paciência.
'Recommend' é aconselhar; 'recommend patience' é aconselhar a paciência.

questions.q: 'Encourage truth' and 'recommend patience' have something in common. What is it?
options: Both are done in relation to other people

questions.q: Verse 2 is a general claim. How does verse 3 change it?
options: It limits it with an exception made of four actions
It asks a question about it
It moves it to the past
questions.why: 'Except those who...' tira da afirmação do versículo 2 quem faz as quatro coisas.

questions.q: Which statement is best supported by the text?
options: It states a general condition and then limits it with an exception
It tells a story with characters
It gives a list of places
It has no connection between its verses

C1.discussion: The passage states a loss and then an exception in very few words. How does this compact order shape the reader's attention?
C1.writing: Write 120 to 150 words: Explain how verse 3 limits the statement in verse 2.

questions.q: Which word introduces the exception in verse 3?

options: an exception to the general claim in verse 2
questions.why: A expressão marca uma excepção à afirmação do versículo 2.

questions.q: Verse 2 names only the human being and loss. What does the lack of detail do?
options: It states the claim in its plainest and most general form, leaving verse 3 to supply the exception
questions.why: O versículo 2 é curto e geral, e o versículo 3 completa-o com a excepção.

questions.q: Which pattern do the actions in verse 3 follow?
questions.why: 'Believe', 'do good works', 'encourage truth' e 'recommend patience' são ligados por 'and'.

options: A short opening, a general claim, and an exception built as a list of four parallel actions
questions.why: Versículo 1: abertura curta. Versículo 2: afirmação geral. Versículo 3: excepção em lista de quatro acções.

C2.discussion: The exception in verse 3 is longer than the claim it limits. What effect does that imbalance have?
C2.writing: Write 150 to 200 words: Analyse how the three verses are built, referring to specific words and to the pattern of claim and exception.
